title: Fugaro routing ls
description: The document `fugaro routing ls --json` prints: the selected project's routing table — the `model_routing:` block of the installation's own config — and, for every model a run of the project can be served on, the entry that answers it and why that entry won. The read is offline: it reaches no bucket, no database and no host, and what it says about the cloud is what the local files already say. Members are only ever added within a version (D784), so a renamed or re-meant member is a new member under a new name and the old one is kept, and removing or retyping one bumps version. No object here is closed for that reason: additionalProperties is left true everywhere, because a consumer that refused a member this schema does not know would refuse a newer CLI's document, which D784 promises to keep readable under the same version.

project.description: The selected project's name. Absent when no project config was selected, which leaves entries and models empty.

entries.description: The table, in the order the project wrote it. Empty is a project that has published no table, where every model a run can call is refused (R1, R22).

models.description: One row per model a run of this project can be served on, in the order the crafts resolve: the five crafts' resolved models, the four models agent.models pins, and each review level's agent.levels.<level>.model. The rungs decided per launch — a task's own grade, a --model override — are not here, because no file names them.

match.description: The model or pattern this entry answers: an exact ID, or a prefix ending in *. The most specific match wins (D3172).

chain.description: The entry's sources, first usable one wins, each spelled the way `fugaro routing set` takes them, so what this document prints is what that command accepts.

sources.description: The same chain in the table's own members, so a reader that has to tell a pool from a provider reads them apart rather than parsing the spelling above.

source.description: This source spelled the way `fugaro routing set` takes it: the kind, the name the kind carries, and @MODEL after either for a written downgrade.

kind.description: routing.Kinds, the closed set of credential sources. A sixth kind is a change to internal/routing/table.go and to every reader's switch.

pool.description: The project's pool name, on a source of kind pool and on no other.

provider.description: The provider entry's name, on a source of kind provider and on no other.

model.description: The model this source serves when the call asked for another one — a written downgrade, which spec.md requires to be explicit. Absent means the model the call asked for.

admit.description: The repositories this source may serve (D3182), on the kinds that are a single credential of the project. An empty or absent list admits nobody: the fail-closed direction. A pool carries no list here — its admission is its members' own.

crafts.description: The crafts that run this model, in config.CraftNames' order. Empty for a model only a pin or a review level names.

entry.description: The match of the entry that wins for this model (routing.Resolve). Absent when no entry matches, which is a run that cannot start; `why` says so.

why.description: Why that entry won: the only entry that matches, the longest of several patterns, an exact ID over the patterns that also match, or — with no entry at all — why none did.
